label: vulnerable
description: Renamed standardBrowserEnv/msie/urlParsingNode/originURL/resolveURL/url/href/requestURL/parsed -> pageOriginProbe/isLegacyIE/anchor/pageOrigin/parseWithAnchor/rawUrl/resolved/target/candidate (object-literal keys, regex literals and string literals untouched). The flagged pattern (untrusted URL written into a DOM <a> via setAttribute('href', ...) to decide the origin) is unchanged. Verified in jsdom: identical answers to the original on all 15 inputs.
notes: DISPUTED ADVISORY. The CVE-2024-57965 / GHSA-fh7x-2848-jmpf text says the code 'does not use a URL object when determining an origin, and has a potentially unwanted setAttribute('href',href) call. NOTE: some parties feel that the code change only addresses a warning message from a SAST tool and does not fix a vulnerability.' Empirical check (jsdom, 14 string URLs including protocol-relative, embedded credentials, javascript:, data:, backslash forms and default ports): the old and new logic give IDENTICAL answers; the only difference found is a non-string object input (old code trusts its fields, new code stringifies it). No exploit was reproduced. The 'vulnerable' label therefore rests on the advisory's stated pattern (DOM-anchor href parsing instead of a URL object), not on a demonstrated exploit. The located 'function' is the module's whole export-default conditional expression (a default-export IIFE), not a named function.

The overload is renamed by this variant only; Javadoc {@link ...} references elsewhere in the file still name correctlySpends and are left as-is (comments). Live verification used bitcoinj-core 0.17.1 (the real vulnerable file compiles cleanly against it), with real ECKey signatures over the real legacy and witness sighashes.

Verified with real bitcoinj: the owner's own spends are accepted and the attacker's spend of both output types is rejected, matching the upstream-patched method.

Because the safe variant fixes both, no 'safe' file carries an unfixed leak. Test-stub observation: the upstream-patched getAppSettings still returns jwtSecret if the settings document contains it (updateAppSettings deletes jwtSecret, which suggests it does); the safe variant masks it.

description: Standalone getPublicBranding() with the same res.success({ msg, data }) shape over the stored settings, but the response is built by picking an explicit allow-list of public branding fields, so no secret can be in it and later-added secret fields are excluded by default.

label: vulnerable
description: Renamed processInitialRequest -> handleHandshakeInit (definition and its single call site in the message dispatch switch) and message/now/certificatesToInclude/initialResponseMessage/cb -> incoming/timestamp/certsToSend/replyMessage/handler, including the template-literal interpolation ${message.initialNonce} and the two type-annotated declarations (all three had to be renamed by hand; sessionNonce and signature are object-literal shorthand properties and were deliberately kept). The exact vulnerability (string-concatenate two base64 values, then decode once) is unchanged. Verified with the real ts-sdk source tree: type-checks with 0 errors; a crafted peer nonce with '=' padding makes the responder sign only 32 bytes, dropping its own 48-byte session nonce.
notes: Measured behavior (real ts-sdk 1.9.30 source, ProtoWallet crypto): with honest, SDK-generated nonces (48 bytes = 64 unpadded base64 chars) ALL versions sign and verify 96 bytes and the handshake completes -- the string-concatenation bug is only reachable through the PEER-CHOSEN initialNonce. With a padded peer nonce (32 bytes -> 44 chars ending '=') the vulnerable code signs only 32 bytes (the responder's session nonce is dropped); the fix signs 80. The upstream-patched file leaves processInitialResponse's identical string concatenation unchanged, but there the first part is the local unpadded nonce, so it was not shown independently exploitable, and honest handshakes with the patched signing side still complete. Lesson recorded in the build script: this case's renamed variant initially referenced undefined names because template-literal interpolations and type-annotated declarations defeat the string/key-protecting rename rule; caught by tsc and the live test.

label: vulnerable
description: Moves the concatenate-then-decode expression into a new private async helper handshakeData(initialNonce, sessionNonce); the string concatenation before decoding is unchanged, so the vulnerability is unchanged. Verified with the real ts-sdk: 0 type errors; same 32-byte signed data for the padded peer nonce.

label: safe
description: Decodes each nonce on its own and joins the BYTES with Array.concat (upstream uses a spread of two decoded arrays) in processInitialRequest, and does the same in the sibling processInitialResponse's dataToVerify (which upstream left unchanged) so no concatenate-then-decode remains. Verified with the real ts-sdk: 0 type errors; a full two-peer handshake still completes (96 bytes signed and verified) and the crafted padded peer nonce now yields 80 signed bytes (32 + 48), i.e. both nonces, identical to the upstream-patched file.

label: safe
description: Standalone joinFixedLengthNonces() with the same 'concatenate two base64 strings, then decode once' pattern, but it accepts only exactly 40-character unpadded values (30 bytes, no '='), and refuses everything else, so decoding the concatenation equals decoding each and joining the bytes and nothing can be dropped.

label: vulnerable
description: Renamed the static method parse_native_url -> parse_ifttt_webhook_url (no in-file callers; the plugin loader calls it by name) and url/result -> raw_url/found (regex text untouched). The exact vulnerability (nested quantifier ([A-Z0-9_-]+/?)+ over an ambiguous body) is unchanged. Verified with Python's re engine: same outputs as the original on 10 URLs, and on webhook + 'A'*N + '!' the time grows exponentially (0.02 s at N=16, 0.33 s at N=20, 5.3 s at N=24, over 8 s at N=28).

The safe variant preserves the original output exactly. Timing harness note: an earlier attempt used the shell `timeout` command, which does not exist on macOS, and its 'TIMEOUT' lines were discarded; the numbers recorded here come from subprocess.run(timeout=8).

Earlier draft of the policy helper used Character.isWhitespace and disagreed with the regex on exotic Unicode whitespace (19,526 of 400,000 adversarial strings); fixed to the regex's own definition before this record.

notes: Measured on this machine (JDK 26, macOS, umask 022): File.createTempFile -> rw-r--r--, Files.createTempFile -> rw-------. The vulnerability therefore depends on the process umask and the platform: with umask 077 File.createTempFile would also produce owner-only files, which is why the finding is a default-permissions weakness rather than an unconditional exposure. The temp directory itself (java.io.tmpdir) was not changed by any variant.

description: Renames the local nioOutAppBuf to pooledPlainBuf at all seven uses in unwrap (whole-method replacement); unwrap keeps its name and signature (private, called by decode). The retry-on-BUFFER_OVERFLOW loop with the fixed pooled buffer is unchanged.
notes: Measured caveat: with a plaintext record (20,000 bytes) much larger than its ciphertext (35 bytes), the upstream-patched code no longer spins but throws IndexOutOfBoundsException at nettyOutAppBuf.writeBytes(outAppBuf), because the Netty output buffer is still created with initialNettyOutAppBufCapacity (the ciphertext length) and not grown; the safe variant sizes it with Math.max(initialNettyOutAppBufCapacity, outAppBuf.remaining()) so the record is delivered. description: In create_client_files renames the locals ca_file/key_file/cert_file to ca_handle/key_handle/cert_handle (whole identifiers; the cached_*_file path variables are untouched); the function keeps its name and signature. The chmod calls still come after all three writes.
notes: Measured caveat: the upstream order still creates the file with the umask mode and tightens it a moment later (a process that opens the file in that instant keeps a readable descriptor to a file that later receives the key); the safe variant creates each file with os.open(..., O_RDWR|O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 0o600) so it never exists with wider permissions. The same open/write/chmod sequence appears for all three files (CA, key, certificate) in the if-not-isdir branch, and the tempfile branch (NamedTemporaryFile, created 0o600) is not affected. Note the chmod-after order leaves every final mode 0o600, which is why the vulnerability is a race window rather than a persistent misconfiguration; the temporary directory itself is created by os.mkdir (default 0o755).

description: In remove_logical_volumes renames the local lvremove to removal_cmd; the function keeps its name and *paths signature (called by name from the libvirt driver). Only lvremove runs, no zero fill.
notes: Measured caveat: the upstream clear_logical_volume uses / where Python 2 integer division was intended (zero_blocks = remaining_bytes / bs, bs /= 1024); under Python 3 it yields float block counts and seeks that dd would reject, so the harness emulates Python 2 by turning ' / ' and ' /= ' into floor division in the harness copy of the extracted functions only (shipped files untouched). The safe variant uses divmod, which behaves the same on Python 2 and 3, and issues two dd commands (bs=1 MiB with oflag=direct for the whole blocks, bs=1 for the tail). remove_logical_volumes is the only place in the file that deletes logical volumes, so there is no sibling site. The replay checks the arguments' arithmetic, not a real block device.

notes: Measured caveat: os.makedirs(path, 0o700) still goes through the process umask and applies the mode only to the leaf directory (intermediate directories get the default), and the upstream-fixed code still creates the file with the umask mode for an instant before os.chmod, while the safe variant creates the file with os.open(..., mode) and also chmods an already existing file, so it never exists with wider permissions; it treats an unparsable permission string as 0o600. The 'executable code run as root in the container' framing comes from the storlets design, not from this harness, which measures modes only.

description: In _download_image_to_temp renames the locals r->resp, ext->file_ext and tf->out (the data: branch is untouched); the function keeps its name and signature (called from the DOCX and PPTX builders). requests.get(src) is still called on any URL.
